description: Experience the rich and creamy delight of classic Indian Butter Chicken, also known as Murgh Makhani. This beloved dish features tender chicken pieces simmered in a luscious tomato-based gravy, enriched with butter, cream, and aromatic spices. Perfect for a comforting meal, it promises an explosion of authentic Indian flavors that will tantalize your taste buds.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1 tsp garam masala, and salt. Mix well to ensure all chicken pieces are coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, reduce heat to medium and add 2 tbsp butter. Once melted, add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Base
instructions.text: Pour in the crushed tomatoes, 1/2 tsp sugar, and salt to taste. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to break down further. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Blend the Sauce to Smoothness
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the cooked tomato and onion mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender directly in the pot. Blend until completely smooth. Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture, pressing down on solids to extract all liquid.

instructions.title: Finish the Butter Chicken Sauce
instructions.text: Return the smooth sauce to the pan over medium-low heat. Stir in the cashew paste and 1/4 cup heavy cream. Add the cooked chicken back into the sauce. Crush the kasuri methi between your palms and add it to the curry. Stir gently to combine.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Let the butter chicken simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the flavors and the sauce to thicken slightly. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish with a swirl of extra cream, a pat of butter, and fresh chopped cilantro before serving hot with naan bread, roti, or steamed basmati rice.

tips: For an extra rich and smoky flavor, char the marinated chicken in a tandoor or under a broiler for a few minutes before adding to the sauce.
Soak cashews in hot water for 15-20 minutes before blending to ensure a super smooth and creamy cashew paste for the sauce.
Butter Chicken tastes even better the next day! Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop.
article:
## Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani (Indian Chicken Recipes)

Few dishes capture the heart and soul of Indian cuisine quite like Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani). A global phenomenon, this iconic dish is celebrated for its incredibly rich, creamy, and subtly spiced tomato-based gravy, tender chicken, and comforting warmth. It’s a culinary masterpiece that has delighted palates worldwide, from bustling street food stalls in Delhi to fine dining establishments across continents. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality flavor in your own kitchen, you're in the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know about making the classic Murgh Makhani, ensuring a delicious and authentic experience.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

At its core, Butter Chicken is a triumph of creamy, mildly spiced tomato gravy with succulent pieces of tandoor-cooked or pan-fried chicken. The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter," a fitting description for a dish that generously incorporates butter and cream, creating its signature velvety texture and luxurious mouthfeel.

Its origins trace back to the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, India, in the 1950s, post-partition. Legend has it that the chefs, needing a way to use leftover tandoori chicken and keep it moist, created a rich tomato and butter-based gravy. This ingenious improvisation quickly became a sensation, cementing Murgh Makhani's place in the pantheon of Indian culinary greats. The distinct flavor profile comes from a blend of aromatic spices like garam masala, kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), and sometimes a touch of sugar to balance the tanginess of the tomatoes. It’s a dish that embodies comfort, elegance, and the vibrant flavors of India.

## Ingredients You'll Need for Butter Chicken

Crafting the perfect Murgh Makhani requires a thoughtful selection of fresh ingredients for both the chicken marinade and the rich gravy. Here's a breakdown of what you'll need, setting you on the path to creating authentic Butter Chicken.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken (thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces)
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Gravy:
*   2 tbsp butter
*   1 tbsp oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (400g) can crushed tomatoes or 3-4 large fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup raw cashews, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes (optional, but adds richness)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or cashew cream for a dairy-free option)
*   1 tbsp kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), lightly crushed
*   1 tsp sugar (or to taste, balances tang)
*   1 tsp red chili powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   Salt to taste
*   Water or chicken broth, as needed for consistency
*   Fresh coriander leaves, for garnish

## How to Make Butter Chicken: Step-by-Step Guide

Mastering homemade Butter Chicken is a rewarding culinary journey. Follow these steps for a truly memorable dish:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, to allow the flavors to penetrate.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned and slightly charred on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. The chicken doesn’t need to be cooked through at this stage, as it will finish cooking in the gravy. Remove the chicken and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In the same pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Add Tomatoes and Spices:** Pour in the crushed tomatoes (or fresh puree). If using soaked cashews, drain them and add them to the pan now. Stir in the red chili powder, garam masala, and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes, allowing the tomatoes to break down and the oil to separate from the mixture.
5.  **Blend the Gravy:** Carefully transfer the cooked tomato-onion mixture to a blender (or use an immersion blender directly in the pot). Blend until perfectly smooth. This step is crucial for achieving the signature silky texture of Murgh Makhani. Strain the gravy back into the pan through a fine-mesh sieve for an extra-smooth consistency, pressing down on any solids.
6.  **Simmer and Finish:** Return the smooth gravy to the pan over low-medium heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces. Stir in the kasoori methi (crushed between your palms to release its aroma) and sugar. If the gravy is too thick, add a splash of water or chicken broth to reach your desired consistency. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, allowing the chicken to finish cooking and absorb the flavors of the gravy.
7.  **Add Cream and Serve:** Finally, stir in the heavy cream. Cook for just a couple of minutes more, being careful not to boil the gravy once the cream is added, as it can curdle. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves.

## Pro Tips for the Best Murgh Makhani

Achieving that authentic restaurant-quality taste for your Murgh Makhani is all about paying attention to a few key details:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will become. Overnight marination in the fridge yields the best results.
*   **Char the Chicken:** If possible, cook your marinated chicken in a tandoor or grill for that smoky, charred flavor. If not, pan-frying until slightly browned and caramelized will add depth that boiling or baking won't.
*   **Smooth Gravy is Essential:** For a truly luxurious texture, blend your gravy base until absolutely smooth. Straining it through a fine-mesh sieve afterward removes any tiny bits of onion or tomato skin, resulting in an incredibly silky consistency.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Use good quality canned tomatoes or ripe, flavorful fresh tomatoes. Fresh ginger and garlic paste made at home will always outperform store-bought versions.
*   **Don't Skip Kasoori Methi:** Dried fenugreek leaves are a signature ingredient in Butter Chicken. Crushing them between your palms before adding them releases their unique, slightly bitter and aromatic flavor, which is indispensable.
*   **Balance the Flavors:** Butter Chicken should have a delicate balance of sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy. Adjust the sugar and chili powder to your preference. A little sweetness balances the acidity of the tomatoes beautifully.
*   **Low and Slow with Cream:** When adding cream, keep the heat low and stir gently. Avoid vigorous boiling after adding cream to prevent it from curdling.

## Serving Suggestions for Butter Chicken

The rich, velvety texture of Butter Chicken begs for the perfect accompaniment to soak up every last drop of its delicious gravy. Here are some classic serving suggestions:

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, chewy, and slightly charred naan bread is arguably the most popular choice. Garlic naan or butter naan elevate the experience even further.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a neutral base that perfectly complements the rich flavors of the Murgh Makhani.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** For a lighter option, whole wheat roti or flaky paratha are excellent choices.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber raita (yogurt dip) can offer a refreshing contrast to the richness of the Butter Chicken.
*   **Simple Salad:** A side of sliced red onions, cucumbers, and tomatoes with a squeeze of lemon juice adds freshness and crunch.
*   **Pickles:** Indian mango or lime pickles can provide a zesty, spicy kick that some enjoy alongside their meal.

## Variations and Substitutions for Murgh Makhani

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect as is, it's also wonderfully adaptable to different dietary needs and preferences:

*   **Dairy-Free Butter Chicken:** For a dairy-free version, substitute plain yogurt with a dairy-free alternative (like coconut yogurt) in the marinade. Replace butter with a plant-based butter or coconut oil, and use full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream instead of heavy cream in the gravy.
*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Easily transform this dish into a vegetarian delight by substituting chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower and potatoes. Simply pan-fry your chosen substitute and add it to the simmering gravy.
*   **Spiciness Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to suit your heat preference. For a milder dish, reduce the amount or use Kashmiri chili powder, which provides color with less heat. For more spice, add a finely chopped green chili along with the ginger-garlic paste.
*   **Nut Alternatives:** If you have a cashew allergy, blanched almonds (soaked and pureed) can be used as a substitute to provide richness and thickness to the gravy.
*   **Tomato Options:** While canned crushed tomatoes offer convenience and consistent flavor, fresh, ripe plum tomatoes, pureed and strained, can also be used for a brighter, fresher taste.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** A traditional touch involves placing a small, hot piece of charcoal in a small metal bowl within the gravy, drizzling a little ghee over it, and quickly covering the pot to infuse a smoky aroma (Dhungar method).

Making your own Butter Chicken is an experience that brings the magic of Indian flavors right to your table. With this detailed guide, you're now equipped to create a classic Murgh Makhani that will impress family and friends, offering a taste of India's most beloved chicken curry. Enjoy the rich, aromatic journey!
